title: Secrets
searchPlaceholder: Search secrets by name or description

badges.systemHint: Managed by McHarbor for the {{module}} module. Change it where that module configures it.
badges.staleHint_one: {{count}} resource still runs an older value. The secret is on version {{version}}.
badges.staleHint_other: {{count}} resources still run an older value. The secret is on version {{version}}.

empty.title: No secrets yet
empty.description: Store a credential once and reference it from any stack as ${secret:NAME}. It is encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser.

fields.name: Name
fields.nameHint: Uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Reference it as ${secret:NAME}.
fields.scopeHint: A stack secret overrides an environment one, which overrides a global one, which overrides an application one. Application is for credentials McHarbor itself uses.
fields.globalDenied: Creating a secret every environment can read requires the {{permission}} permission.
fields.autoApplyHint: Recreates containers and redeploys stacks as soon as this secret is rotated. Off by default, because applying restarts whatever uses it.
fields.groupHint: Optional. A free-text label used only to organise this list — it is not part of the secret’s name and does not change what ${secret:NAME} resolves to.
fields.kindHint: Presentation only — every kind is stored and resolved the same way. Pick one, or type a name to add your own.

create.title: New secret
create.description: The value is encrypted at rest and never returned by the list or detail endpoints.
create.shownOnce: Copy this now — it is shown once

rotate.title: Rotate secret
rotate.description: Replaces the value of {{name}}. The previous value is kept so the rotation can be rolled back.

rotation.title: {{name}} was rotated
rotation.body_one: {{count}} resource still runs the old value. A rotation takes effect when it is recreated or redeployed.
rotation.body_other: {{count}} resources still run the old value. A rotation takes effect when they are recreated or redeployed.
rotation.autoBody_one: Applying to {{count}} resource in the background. This banner clears once it is up to date.
rotation.autoBody_other: Applying to {{count}} resources in the background. This banner clears once they are up to date.

reveal.title: Reveal {{name}}
reveal.description: Show the stored value in plaintext.
reveal.auditedBody: Your username, the reason you give, your IP address and the time are written to the audit log before the value is shown. Administrators are notified.
reveal.reasonHint: At least 10 characters. Recorded verbatim in the audit log.
reveal.reasonPlaceholder: Restoring the database after the failed migration on the staging host
reveal.stepUpHint: Confirm it is you. Either your password or a code from your authenticator app is enough.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}
delete.description: This cannot be undone. The rotation history is deleted with it.
delete.inUseBody: Deleting it will fail the next deploy of everything below, because an unresolved reference stops a deploy rather than substituting an empty value.

actions.revealDenied: Revealing a value requires an approved elevation for secrets.reveal.
actions.revealSystemDenied: Application credentials cannot be revealed here.
actions.promoteBody: The value is stored as a secret and this variable becomes a ${secret:NAME} reference. It will no longer be visible in this editor — reading it again needs an approved elevation.
actions.rotateSystemDenied: Application credentials are rotated where their module configures them.
actions.deleteSystemDenied: Application credentials cannot be deleted here.
actions.editSystemDenied: Application credentials are described by the module that owns them.

insert.title: Insert a secret
insert.description: Pick a stored secret. The field receives a ${secret:NAME} reference — McHarbor substitutes the real value server-side when it deploys.
insert.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, description or stack
insert.emptyDescription: Create one under Security → Secrets, then reference it from here.
insert.noMatchDescription: No stored secret matches that search.
insert.hint: Hold Shift while right-clicking a field to open this picker; a plain right-click keeps your browser's own menu.

fileMode.label: Deliver secrets as files
fileMode.hint: Writes each ${secret:NAME} to /run/secrets and sets <VAR>_FILE to its path, so the resolved value never appears in the container's environment.
fileMode.compatTitle: Only for images that support it
fileMode.compatBody: The image must read the _FILE variant of the variable. Most official database and proxy images do (POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE, MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD_FILE, and similar); images that do not will start without the credential.
fileMode.limitBody: This keeps the value out of `docker inspect` and the process environment. Anyone with access to the Docker socket can still read the file inside the container — the vault raises the bar, it does not remove the daemon's authority.

impact.title: What uses {{name}}
impact.description: The secret is on version {{version}}. Anything below that version still runs an older value.
impact.staleHint: Built with version {{applied}}; the secret is on version {{current}}.
impact.staleUnknownHint: Built before McHarbor recorded secret versions, so it may be running an older value.
impact.staleBody: A rotation changes the stored value and nothing that is already running. Applying recreates containers and redeploys stacks so they pick it up.
impact.unsupportedHint: This resource reads the secret each time it runs, so a rotation already reaches it. There is nothing to restart.
impact.copiedHint: This resource took a one-time copy of the secret when it was created, so rotating the secret does not change it. Change it on the resource itself.
impact.missingHint: The container or stack this reference points at is gone. Nothing to update — the reference is left over.
impact.missingTitle_one: {{count}} reference points at something that is gone
impact.missingTitle_other: {{count}} references point at something that is gone
impact.missingBody: Left behind by containers that were recreated or removed. They cannot be updated and inflate nothing but the noise.

apply.warning: Applying restarts each resource in turn. A failure does not stop the run — every resource is attempted and reported separately.
apply.failedBody: The run finished; the resources marked failed still hold the old value. If every one failed, suspect the rotated value itself. The server log has the reason.

edit.title: Edit details
edit.description: Change the group and description of {{name}}. The value is not touched.
